title: Antidepressants at the monoamine synapse
ariaLabel: Schematic of a serotonin or noradrenaline synapse: nerve firing releases transmitter into the cleft, the transporter takes most of it back into the terminal where monoamine oxidase breaks it down, and what stays in the cleft stimulates postsynaptic receptors. SSRIs, SNRIs and tricyclics block the transporter, MAO inhibitors raise the amount stored and released, and alpha-2 antagonists such as mirtazapine raise release by blocking the autoreceptor.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or level is shown or implied.

drugs.label: SSRI or SNRI type (blocks the transporter)
NDRI (bupropion type, blocks dopamine and noradrenaline uptake)

readout: transmitter in the cleft {0} · postsynaptic stimulation {1}
tests: transmitter in the cleft usual · postsynaptic stimulation usual
transmitter in the cleft raised · postsynaptic stimulation raised
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, so more transmitter is left in the cleft or more is stored.
enhanceInfo: A drug of the chosen class increasing this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape): more transmitter is released, either because more is stored (MAO inhibitors) or because the brake of the alpha-2 autoreceptor is removed.

nodes.label: Nerve firing
nodes.info: Impulses in a serotonin (raphe) or noradrenaline (locus coeruleus) neuron. The slider sets how active the neuron is.

nodes.label: Released into the cleft
nodes.info: Transmitter released from vesicles into the synaptic cleft. Alpha-2 autoreceptors on the terminal normally hold release back.

nodes.label: Taken back up
nodes.info: Reuptake by the serotonin transporter (SERT) or noradrenaline transporter (NET) ends most of the signal.

nodes.label: Broken down
nodes.info: Monoamine oxidase on mitochondria in the terminal breaks down the transmitter that is not stored again.

nodes.label: Left in the cleft
nodes.info: The transmitter that is not taken back up stays in the cleft and reaches the receptors.

nodes.label: Postsynaptic receptors
nodes.info: Serotonin and noradrenaline receptors on the next neuron. Clinical benefit takes weeks and involves adaptations beyond this first effect (not drawn).

edges.label: release
edges.info: Release. Alpha-2 autoreceptors on the terminal slow it; mirtazapine blocks them and so increases release. MAO inhibitors stop breakdown inside the terminal, so more transmitter is stored and released.

edges.label: SERT / NET
edges.info: The transporters. SSRIs block the serotonin transporter, SNRIs both, and tricyclic drugs both (with other receptor effects not drawn).
What is not taken back up stays in the cleft.

edges.label: MAO
edges.info: Monoamine oxidase. MAO inhibitors block it, so less is destroyed in the terminal and more is stored.
Transmitter in the cleft stimulates the postsynaptic receptors.

sources: Where each class acts. SSRIs and SNRIs block the serotonin or noradrenaline transporters, tricyclics block both, MAO inhibitors block monoamine oxidase so that more transmitter is stored and released, and mirtazapine blocks alpha-2 autoreceptors and so increases release. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Receptor blockade by tricyclics and mirtazapine (muscarinic, histamine, alpha-1, 5-HT2 and 5-HT3), the delay of weeks before benefit and the adaptations behind it, neurotrophic and other hypotheses of depression, the serotonin syndrome, the tyramine reaction with MAO inhibitors, discontinuation, bupropion and other agents, and the difference between serotonin and noradrenaline neurons are left out. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them. Bupropion is drawn as a reuptake blocker; trazodone, vortioxetine receptor actions, esketamine and agomelatine are not drawn.
